items.stem: Conclusion : Plants exhibit growth and movement in response to stimuli like gravity and light. (iv) Which structure do the remaining parts of flower develop into? (v) Can you notice a pod or a fruit with seeds develop from a flower? (vi) What happens to the plant after the fruits containing seeds are formed? Table : Changes observed during the growth of the plant Date Observations Sketches Seeds are sown
items.answer: Date Observations Sketches (Conceptual descriptions) Day 1 Seeds are sown. Small, oval bean seed. Day 3-5 Seed swells, root emerges. Seed with a tiny white root pointing down. Day 6-8 Shoot emerges, tiny leaves appear. Root growing down, small green shoot with two tiny leaves pointing up. Day 10-15 Plant grows taller, more leaves develop. Taller plant with several green leaves on a thin stem. Day 20-30 Stem thickens, plant gets bushier. Stronger stem, more branches and leaves. Day 40-50 Flower buds appear. Plant with small, unopened flower buds. Day 50-60 First flowers bloom. Plant with open flowers. Day 65-75 Flowers dry and pods (fruits) start to form. Dried flowers, tiny green pods appearing where flowers were. Day 80-90 Pods grow larger, seeds develop inside. Large green pods on the plant. Day 90+ Plant starts to turn yellow, pods mature and dry. Plant showing signs of yellowing leaves, dry pods. Day 100- 110 Plant dries out and dies after seeds are fully formed. Dried, shriveled plant with mature, dry pods. (i) The first changes (swelling of seed, emergence of root) can occur within 3 to 5 days, depending on the conditions. (ii) The first flower typically appears around 40- 60 days after sowing the seed. (iii) Yes, after the flower dries, the ovary part of the flower starts to grow and swell. This is where the fruit (pod) will form. (iv) The remaining parts of the flower (specifically the ovary) develop into the fruit (in this case, the bean pod). (v) Yes, a green pod (fruit) will develop from the flower, and if you open it later, you will find new bean seeds inside. (vi) After the fruits (pods) with mature seeds are formed, the bean plant usually completes its life cycle. It will start to turn yellow, dry out, and eventually die. This is because its main purpose, which is to produce new seeds for the next generation, has been fulfilled. Activity 10.5 : Let us analyse Let us solve an interesting puzzle. How will you decide which stage (larva or pupa) comes immediately after the egg stage? Suppose you are given a container with water from a puddle containing larvae and pupae. Design an activity to find out the correct sequence of these stages. You can take help of the following activity designed by Avadhi to create your own activity- Step 1: I have a water container with mosquito larvae and pupae. Step 2: I will separate 4-5 larvae and pupae into two separate containers with the same water. Step 3: I will observe them every day until I see them changing to the next stage. Step 4: If the larvae change into pupae, it would mean that the larval stage comes before the pupal stage or vice-versa. Step 5: I will keep watching both the containers to see in which one a mosquito appears first. These observations will help us to learn the correct sequence of growth. NCERT ACTIVITY Activity 10.1 : Let us record We are surrounded by numerous things. Just look around in your classroom and you may find many examples-the pencil that you are holding, the book that you are reading or the pigeon near the window.

items.answer: (I) Name (II) My guess (Living/ Non-living) (III) Remarks (Common Class 6 Understanding) Pencil Non-living Does not move on its own, does not grow, does not need food. Book Non-living Does not move, grow, breathe, or eat. Pigeon Living Moves, eats, grows, breathes, makes sounds. Car Non-living Moves, but needs fuel to move, does not grow or reproduce on its own. Plant Living Grows, needs water/ sunlight (food), can move parts like leaves, reproduces (seeds). Your Friend Living Moves, eats, grows, breathes, responds, reproduces. Record your predictions for each pot kept under different conditions in Table. items.answer: Pot with bean seeds Availability Air Availability Sunlight Availability Water Possible Seed germination Prediction Observation (Expected Results) Possible reason for the observation A: In direct sunlight and without water Yes Yes No No No germination Water is essential for germination. Without water, the seed coat won’t soften and the embryo can’t activate. B: In direct sunlight and excess water Limited/No Yes Yes (Excess) No No germination Excess water fills all air spaces in the soil, preventing the seeds from getting enough air, which is necessary for respiration during germination. D: In direct sunlight and moist soil Yes Yes Yes (Moderate) Yes Germination All essential conditions (air and water) are met for germination. Light is not an inhibitor for bean seeds. items.stem: General Conclusion : Plants and animals undergo unique life cycles with significant changes, essential for survival and continuity. Protecting their habitats is important. Figure : Life cycle of a frog Now, suppose you are given a container filled with water from a puddle which contains larvae and pupae. Without separating them from the container, how would you design an activity to decide which stage, out of the two, gives way to the next? Figure : Life cycle of a mosquito
items.answer: From these observations, you can conclude the correct sequence: Egg → Larva → Pupa → Adult This means larva comes immediately after the egg, followed by the pupa stage, and then the adult mosquito. Activity 10.6 : Let us analyse Avadhi and Aayush are dressed up in full sleeves shirts and full pants today. It has been raining intermittently for a week. They are going out with their classmates for an activity. After a brief walk led by their science teacher, they reach a shallow pond. It is surrounded by trees and tall grasses. The teacher cautions them to watch everything from a distance without causing any disturbance. You may also go to a small water body during the rainy season with a facilitator and explore it by taking due safety precautions. You may notice a white jelly-like substance on the surface of water towards the edge of the pond (Figure). This may also be attached to plants growing in or around the water. This jelly-like substance is actually a cluster of eggs of a frog and is known as spawn. Observe the features of all the stages of a frog shown in figure . How will you decide the sequence of the given stages (A, B, C, D, E, F)? Some of the stages show distinct changes in their initial and final shapes. Record these changes in Table. Figure : Different stages of a frog in a pond Table : Changes in different life stages of a frog A B C D E F It is similar to ‘C’ but it has two legs.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes the characteristics that set living beings apart from non-living things, as discussed ?

options.label: A
options.text: Living beings are always larger than non- living things

options.label: B
options.text: Living beings can move, need food, grow, respire, excrete, respond, reproduce, and die

options.label: C
options.text: Non-living things can reproduce, but living beings cannot

options.label: D
options.text: Only living beings are made of complex materials

items.answer: (B) Living beings can move, need food, grow, respire, excrete, respond, reproduce, and die. The outlines several key characteristics common to living beings, including movement, nutrition, growth, respiration, excretion, response to stimuli, reproduction and eventually, death, which differentiate them from non-living things.

items.stem: In the story, what did Avadhi’s mother explain about the shell Avadhi tried to pick up?

options.label: A
options.text: That it was just an empty, non-living object

options.label: B
options.text: That the shell could be home to a living snail and is part of its body

options.label: C
options.text: That shells are too delicate to be touched

options.label: D
options.text: That the shell was a rare type of rock formation

items.answer: (B) That the shell could be home to a living snail and is part of its body. Avadhi’s mother advised her not to pick up the shell because it could contain a living snail and that the shell itself is actually a part of the snail’s body.

items.stem: Why is a car, despite being able to move, generally classified as non-living?

options.label: A
options.text: Because it does not consume fuel to move

options.label: B
options.text: Because it cannot move on its own without a driver or engine

options.label: C
options.text: Because it does not exhibit other characteristics of living beings like growth, reproduction, or respiration

options.label: D
options.text: Because it is made of metal and plastic

items.answer: (C) Because it does not exhibit other characteristics of living beings like growth, reproduction, or respiration. While a car can move, it lacks other fundamental characteristics of life such as growth from within, the ability to reproduce, respiration, and response to stimuli in a biological sense.

items.stem: What is a stimulus in the context of living beings?

options.label: A
options.text: The food that a living being consumes for energy

options.label: B
options.text: Any thing or event that prompts a living being to respond

options.label: C
options.text: The process of breathing in air

options.label: D
options.text: The growth of a plant towards sunlight

items.answer: (B) Any thing or event that prompts a living being to respond. A stimulus is any change or event in the internal or external environment that can elicit a reaction or response from a living organism. Examples include light, sound, touch or temperature changes.

items.stem: Which plant is mentioned as an example that folds its leaves when touched?

options.label: A
options.text: Rose plant

options.label: B
options.text: Mango tree

options.label: C
options.text: Touch-me-not (mimosa, chhui-mui)

options.label: D
options.text: Grass

items.answer: (C) Touch-me-not (mimosa, chhui-mui) The chapter provides the touch-me-not plant (also known by its various local names) as an example of a plant that responds to the stimulus of touch by folding its leaves.

items.stem: What is the primary purpose of reproduction in living beings?

options.label: A
options.text: To allow individual organisms to grow larger

options.label: B
options.text: To ensure the continuity of life for that species

options.label: C
options.text: To help organisms respond to their environment

options.label: D
options.text: To provide food for other organisms

items.answer: (B) To ensure the continuity of life for that species. Reproduction is the biological process by which new individual organisms – offspring – are produced from their parent or parents. This process is essential for the continuation and survival of a species across generations.

items.stem: What is excretion in living beings?

options.label: A
options.text: The process of taking in food for energy

options.label: B
options.text: The process of breathing to obtain oxygen

options.label: C
options.text: The removal of waste products from the body

options.label: D
options.text: The movement of an organism from one place to another

items.answer: (C) The removal of waste products from the body. Excretion is a vital biological process where metabolic waste products and other non-useful materials are eliminated from an organism’s body to maintain internal balance.

items.stem: What are the tiny pores on the surface of leaves that help plants in taking air in and out called?

options.label: A
options.text: Roots

options.label: B
options.text: Stems

options.label: C
options.text: Stomata

options.label: D
options.text: Petals

items.answer: (C) Stomata Stomata are small pores, typically found on the surface of leaves (and sometimes stems), which facilitate gas exchange (like intake of carbon dioxide and release of oxygen and water vapour) in plants.

items.stem: How does the movement of most plants differ from the movement of most animals?

options.label: A
options.text: Plants cannot move at all, while animals can move freely

options.label: B
options.text: Plants generally do not move from one place to another, but show movements like opening of flowers; animals can move from place to place

options.label: C
options.text: Animals show growth movements, while plants move for food

options.label: D
options.text: Both plants and animals move from place to place in search of sunlight

items.answer: (B) Plants generally do not move from one place to another, but show movements like opening of flowers; animals can move from place to place. Most animals exhibit locomotion (moving from one location to another). Plants are typically rooted but show other types of movements, such as flowers opening/closing or growth towards light.

items.stem: If a bean seed is sown in a pot with moist soil and kept in direct sunlight, and another is kept in complete darkness with moist soil, which condition is primarily being tested for its effect on germination in this comparison?

options.label: A
options.text: The need for soil

options.label: B
options.text: The need for air

options.label: C
options.text: The need for sunlight for germination

options.label: D
options.text: The need for water for germination

items.answer: (C) The need for sunlight for germination. By keeping all other conditions (soil, moisture, likely air) similar and varying only the presence or absence of light, this setup is designed to investigate whether sunlight is an essential condition for the initial process of seed germination.

items.stem: What are the essential conditions identified for the germination of bean seeds?

options.label: A
options.text: Only sunlight and air

options.label: B
options.text: Only water and soil

options.label: C
options.text: The right amount of water and air

options.label: D
options.text: Only darkness and warmth

items.answer: (C) The right amount of water and air. The bean seeds require both adequate water (not too much or too little) and air for successful germination. Sunlight is found not to be essential for the germination itself.

items.stem: What is the outer covering of a seed called?

options.label: A
options.text: Embryo

options.label: B
options.text: Cotyledon

options.label: C
options.text: Seed coat

options.label: D
options.text: Root cap

items.answer: (C) Seed coat The seed coat is the protective outermost layer of a seed. It helps to shield the inner embryo and stored food from damage and harsh environmental conditions.

items.stem: What does it mean when a seed germinates?

options.label: A
options.text: It produces flowers

options.label: B
options.text: It develops into a fruit

options.label: C
options.text: It turns into a sprout, beginning its growth into a plant

options.label: D
options.text: It becomes dry and dormant

items.answer: (C) It turns into a sprout, beginning its growth into a plant. Germination is the process by which a seed begins to grow and develop into a seedling or young plant, typically marked by the emergence of a sprout.

items.stem: When a plant seedling is kept inverted (shoot downwards, root upwards) in sunlight, how do the shoot and root generally grow?

options.label: A
options.text: The shoot grows downwards, and the root grows upwards

options.label: B
options.text: Both the shoot and root grow sideways

options.label: C
options.text: The shoot bends and grows upwards; the root bends and grows downwards

options.label: D
options.text: The plant stops growing in this position

items.answer: (C) The shoot bends and grows upwards; the root bends and grows downwards. Plants exhibit tropisms. Shoots typically grow upwards (against gravity and often towards light), and roots grow downwards (with gravity). Even if inverted, they will reorient their growth accordingly.

items.stem: Which Indian scientist built a machine called a crescograph to record how plants respond to stimuli?

options.label: A
options.text: C.V. Raman

options.label: B
options.text: Homi J. Bhabha

options.label: C
options.text: Jagadish Chandra Bose

options.label: D
options.text: Salim Ali

items.answer: (C) Jagadish Chandra Bose Jagadish Chandra Bose as the Indian scientist who invented the crescograph. This instrument was used to measure plant growth and their responses to various external stimuli.

items.stem: What is the life cycle of a plant, as described with the bean plant example?

options.label: A
options.text: The daily process of photosynthesis

options.label: B
options.text: The period from when a flower blooms to when it wilts

options.label: C
options.text: The entire process from a seed to a mature plant producing new seeds

options.label: D
options.text: The way a plant’s leaves change color in different seasons

items.answer: (C) The entire process from a seed to a mature plant producing new seeds. The life cycle of a plant encompasses all the stages of its development, starting from a seed, growing into a seedling, maturing into an adult plant, flowering, producing fruits and new seeds, thereby enabling the next generation.

items.stem: A student plants a bean seed. After several weeks, the plant produces flowers, which then develop into pods containing new bean seeds. The original plant eventually becomes yellow and dry. This entire sequence represents:

options.label: A
options.text: Only the germination phase

options.label: B
options.text: A part of the plant’s response to stimuli

options.label: C
options.text: The complete life cycle of the bean plant

options.label: D
options.text: An example of asexual reproduction

items.answer: (C) The complete life cycle of the bean plant. The scenario describes the key stages from seed to germination, growth, flowering, fruit (pod) formation with new seeds, and finally the death of the parent plant, which constitutes a full life cycle.

items.stem: What are the worm-like creatures found in stagnant water, which are distinct life stages of a mosquito, called?

options.label: A
options.text: Caterpillars and cocoons

options.label: B
options.text: Tadpoles and froglets

options.label: C
options.text: Larva and pupa

options.label: D
options.text: Nymphs and adults

items.answer: (C) Larva and pupa The chapter identifies larva and pupa as two different worm-like developmental stages of a mosquito that are commonly found in stagnant water bodies.

items.stem: Why are people advised not to allow water to stagnate in their surroundings, in relation to mosquitoes?

options.label: A
options.text: Stagnant water evaporates too quickly

options.label: B
options.text: Stagnant water is a breeding ground for mosquitoes, where they lay eggs

options.label: C
options.text: Stagnant water attracts birds that eat mosquitoes

options.label: D
options.text: Stagnant water damages the foundations of houses

items.answer: (B) Stagnant water is a breeding ground for mosquitoes, where they lay eggs. Mosquitoes lay their eggs in or near stagnant water. Allowing water to collect and remain still provides an ideal environment for mosquito larvae and pupae to develop, increasing the mosquito population.

items.stem: What is a key difference between the larval stage and the pupal stage of a mosquito, as often observed?

options.label: A
options.text: Larvae can fly, while pupae cannot

options.label: B
options.text: Larvae are found on land, while pupae are in water

options.label: C
options.text: They have different shapes and appearances, with pupae often being more comma-shaped

options.label: D
options.text: Larvae eat plants, while pupae are predatory

items.answer: (C) They have different shapes and appearances, with pupae often being more comma-shaped. The mosquito larva and pupa are visually distinct stages. Larvae are typically elongated and worm- like, while pupae are often more compact and comma-shaped, representing a transformation phase before emerging as an adult.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the four main stages in the life cycle of a mosquito as described in Figure ?

options.label: A
options.text: Egg

options.label: B
options.text: Nymph

options.label: C
options.text: Larva

options.label: D
options.text: Pupa

items.answer: (B) Nymph The mosquito life cycle shown consists of four stages: egg, larva, pupa, and adult. The term nymph is typically used for incomplete metamorphosis in insects like grasshoppers, not mosquitoes.

items.stem: Assertion (A) : Spreading kerosene oil on stagnant water can help control mosquito breeding. Reason (R) : Kerosene oil forms a thin layer that prevents larvae and pupae from inhaling air, causing them to die.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer: (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Mosquito larvae and pupae need to come to the water surface to breathe air. A layer of kerosene oil on the water surface blocks their access to air, leading to their suffocation and death, thus disrupting the mosquito life cycle.

items.stem: They do not respond to stimuli.

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 2 and 3 only

options.label: C
options.text: 1 and 3 only

items.answer: (A) 1 and 2 only Growth and reproduction are fundamental characteristics of living beings. Responding to stimuli is also a key characteristic; not responding would indicate a lack of life or a non-living entity.

items.stem: A gardener notices that the bean seeds sown in a waterlogged pot (excess water) have not germinated well, while those in a pot with moist soil have sprouted. The poor germination in the waterlogged pot is likely because:

options.label: A
options.text: The seeds did not receive enough sunlight

options.label: B
options.text: The seeds lacked sufficient air due to excess water

options.label: C
options.text: The seeds were too old to germinate

options.label: D
options.text: The soil in the waterlogged pot was infertile

items.answer: (B) The seeds lacked sufficient air due to excess water. Seeds require air (oxygen) for respiration during germination. Excess water in the soil fills up air spaces, depriving the seeds of the necessary oxygen, which can inhibit or prevent germination.

items.stem: What is the cluster of frog eggs, often found as a jelly-like substance in water, known as?

options.label: A
options.text: Larva

options.label: B
options.text: Pupa

options.label: C
options.text: Spawn

options.label: D
options.text: Froglet

items.answer: (C) Spawn The jelly-like mass of frog eggs found in or near water as spawn. This is the initial stage of the frog’s life cycle.

items.stem: Why do tadpoles (early stage of a frog) have tails?

options.label: A
options.text: To help them breathe underwater

options.label: B
options.text: To help them swim in water

options.label: C
options.text: To attract mates

options.label: D
options.text: To store food

items.answer: (B) To help them swim in water. Tadpoles are the aquatic larval stage of frogs. Their tails are adapted for propulsion, enabling them to swim effectively in their water habitat before they develop legs and lose their tails.

items.stem: What is a frog let in the life cycle of a frog?

options.label: A
options.text: The adult frog ready to lay eggs

options.label: B
options.text: The earliest egg stage of a frog

options.label: C
options.text: A young frog that still has a tail but has developed legs

options.label: D
options.text: The stage immediately after the egg hatches, without legs

items.answer: (C) A young frog that still has a tail but has developed legs. A frog let is an intermediate stage in frog development. It is a small, young frog that has developed legs but may still retain a tail, transitioning from a fully aquatic tadpole to a more terrestrial adult.

items.stem: How does the habitat of an adult frog generally differ from that of a very young tadpole?

options.label: A
options.text: Adult frogs live only on land; tadpoles live only in trees

options.label: B
options.text: Adult frogs can live both in water and on land; young tadpoles are primarily aquatic

options.label: C
options.text: Adult frogs are purely aquatic; tadpoles live on land

options.label: D
options.text: Both adult frogs and young tadpoles live exclusively on land

items.answer: (B) Adult frogs can live both in water and on land; young tadpoles are primarily aquatic. Young tadpoles are fully aquatic, breathing with gills and swimming with tails. Adult frogs are amphibious, capable of living in water and on land, having developed lungs and legs.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the plant Drovers mentioned in the chapter?

options.label: A
options.text: It is an insectivorous plant

options.label: B
options.text: It has saucer-shaped leaves with hair-like projections

options.label: C
options.text: Its hairs move inward to trap insects with sticky ends

options.label: D
options.text: It primarily obtains nutrition from the soil through its roots

items.answer: (D) It primarily obtains nutrition from the soil through its roots. Drosera is an insectivorous plant, meaning it traps and digests insects to supplement its nutrition, especially in nutrient-poor soils. While it has roots, it relies on insects for certain nutrients.

items.stem: If you wanted to find mosquito larvae and pupae for observation, where would be the most likely place to look?

options.label: A
options.text: In fast-flowing rivers

options.label: B
options.text: In dry, sandy areas

options.label: C
options.text: In stagnant water bodies like puddles or open containers

options.label: D
options.text: On the leaves of tall trees

items.answer: (C) In stagnant water bodies like puddles or open containers. Mosquitoes lay their eggs in still or stagnant water. Therefore, their larval and pupal stages, which are aquatic, are most commonly found in such environments.

items.stem: Assertion (A) : Plants exhibit growth. Reason (R) : Plants require food (nutrition) for their growth and development.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer: (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Growth is a fundamental characteristic of plants. This growth is fueled by nutrients obtained through processes like photosynthesis and absorption from the soil, which provide the energy and building blocks for development.

items.stem: Excess water is always beneficial for germination.

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 2 only

options.label: C
options.text: 1 and 3 only

options.label: D
options.text: 2 and 3 only

items.answer: (B) 2 only The bean seeds need water and air for germination; sunlight is not essential for the germination itself. Excess water can be detrimental by limiting air supply.

items.stem: An insectivorous plant like Drosera traps an insect that lands on its leaves. The movement of the hairs to trap the insect is an example of the plant:

options.label: A
options.text: Reproducing

options.label: B
options.text: Responding to a stimulus (touch and presence of the insect)

options.label: C
options.text: Excreting waste products

options.label: D
options.text: Germinating

items.answer: (B) Responding to a stimulus (touch and presence of the insect) The insect landing on the leaf acts as a stimulus. The plant’s response – the inward movement of its sticky hairs to trap the insect – is a clear example of a living organism responding to an external stimulus.

items.stem: The life cycle of a silk moth, similar to a mosquito, passes through how many distinct life stages mentioned in the Do you know?

options.label: A
options.text: Two stages : egg and adult

options.label: B
options.text: Three stages : egg, larva, and adult

options.label: C
options.text: Four stages : egg, larva, pupa, and adult

options.label: D
options.text: Five stages : egg, young larva, old larva, pupa, and adult

items.answer: (C) Four stages: egg, larva, pupa, and adult. The Do you know? box states that the silk moth also passes through four life stages: egg, larva, pupa, and adult, similar to the complete metamorphosis seen in mosquitoes.

items.stem: Why is the initial stage of a bean plant’s growth from a seed called germination rather than just ‘growth’?

options.label: A
options.text: Because it happens very quickly

options.label: B
options.text: Because it involves the seed transforming into a sprout or seedling

options.label: C
options.text: Because it only occurs in the dark

options.label: D
options.text: Because it does not require any water

items.answer: (B) Because it involves the seed transforming into a sprout or seedling. Germination specifically refers to the process where a dormant seed begins to sprout and develop into a young plant (seedling) under favorable conditions. It’s the initial phase of active growth from a seed.

items.stem: When a living being is no longer able to exhibit essential life characteristics, despite the availability of resources, it is said to be:

options.label: A
options.text: Dormant

options.label: B
options.text: Hibernating

options.label: C
options.text: Dead

options.label: D
options.text: Stimulated

items.answer: (C) Dead Death is defined in the chapter as the state where a living being ceases to show all the essential characteristics of life (like respiration, response, growth), even when necessary resources are present.

items.stem: Which part of the bean seedling typically grows downwards into the soil?

options.label: A
options.text: The shoot

options.label: B
options.text: The leaves

options.label: C
options.text: The root

options.label: D
options.text: The flower

items.answer: (C) The root During germination and subsequent growth, the root of a plant seedling generally grows downwards, anchoring the plant and absorbing water and nutrients from the soil.

items.stem: What is a major difference in the typical habitat of a mosquito larva compared to an adult mosquito?

options.label: A
options.text: Larva is terrestrial; adult is aquatic

options.label: B
options.text: Larva is aquatic; adult is primarily terrestrial (though it needs water for breeding)

options.label: C
options.text: Both larva and adult are exclusively aquatic

options.label: D
options.text: Both larva and adult are exclusively terrestrial

items.answer: (B) Larva is aquatic; adult is primarily terrestrial (though it needs water for breeding). Mosquito larvae are aquatic, living and developing in water. Adult mosquitoes are flying insects that live primarily on land, although females return to water to lay eggs.

items.stem: Which of these is NOT listed as an essential condition affecting the germination of most seeds, as discussed in the chapter (though exceptions exist for light)?

options.label: A
options.text: Availability of water

options.label: B
options.text: Availability of air

options.label: C
options.text: Presence of fertile soil

options.label: D
options.text: Presence of sunlight (for germination itself, not later growth)

items.answer: (D) Presence of sunlight (for germination itself, not later growth). Water and air are essential for bean seed germination. While soil provides a medium, sunlight is generally not required for the germination process of most seeds, though it’s vital for subsequent seedling growth.

items.stem: If a plant’s shoot is observed to bend and grow towards a window, this is a response to which stimulus?

options.label: A
options.text: Gravity

options.label: B
options.text: Touch

options.label: C
options.text: Water

options.label: D
options.text: Light

items.answer: (D) Light Plants often exhibit phototropism, which is the growth response towards a light source. A shoot bending towards a window indicates it is growing towards the sunlight coming from that direction.

items.stem: If seeds are sown in soil that is completely waterlogged (excess water), why might germination be poor or fail?

options.label: A
options.text: The excess water washes away essential nutrients from the seeds

options.label: B
options.text: The seeds do not receive enough air (oxygen) necessary for respiration

options.label: C
options.text: The seeds become too cold in the waterlogged soil

options.label: D
options.text: The excess water makes the seed coat too hard to break

items.answer: (B) The seeds do not receive enough air (oxygen) necessary for respiration. Seeds require oxygen for respiration, which is the process of releasing energy for germination. Waterlogged soil fills air spaces, depriving seeds of oxygen and hindering germination.

items.stem: The part of a germinated seed that develops into the shoot of the plant is called the:

options.label: A
options.text: Root

options.label: B
options.text: Seed coat

options.label: C
options.text: Embryo (specifically the plumule part of the embryo)

options.label: D
options.text: Cotyledon

items.answer: (C) Embryo (specifically the plumule part of the embryo) The embryo within the seed contains the rudimentary parts of the plant. The plumule is the part of the embryo that develops into the shoot (stem and leaves).

items.stem: The life cycle of a mosquito includes an adult stage. Approximately how long may an adult mosquito survive, according to the chapter?

options.label: A
options.text: 1 to 2 days

options.label: B
options.text: 10 to 15 days

options.label: C
options.text: 1 to 2 months

options.label: D
options.text: About a year

items.answer: (B) 10 to 15 days The chapter states that the adult mosquito, after emerging from the pupa, may survive for a period of 10 to 15 days.

items.stem: How does the appearance of a mosquito larva typically differ from that of an adult mosquito?

options.label: A
options.text: Larva has wings and legs; adult is worm-like

options.label: B
options.text: Larva is aquatic and worm-like; adult is a flying insect with wings and legs

options.label: C
options.text: Both larva and adult look identical but differ in size

options.label: D
options.text: Larva is a stationary stage; adult is highly mobile

items.answer: (B) Larva is aquatic and worm-like; adult is a flying insect with wings and legs. Mosquito larvae are aquatic, elongated, and lack wings or fully developed legs. Adult mosquitoes are terrestrial, flying insects with a distinct body structure including wings and legs.

items.stem: Which of these is NOT a characteristic shared by both the life cycle of a mosquito and a silk moth, as mentioned in the chapter?

options.label: A
options.text: Both pass through an egg stage

options.label: B
options.text: Both have a larval stage

options.label: C
options.text: Both have a pupal stage

options.label: D
options.text: Both adult forms are primarily aquatic

items.answer: (D) Both adult forms are primarily aquatic. Both mosquitoes and silk moths undergo complete metamorphosis with egg, larva, pupa, and adult stages. However, adult mosquitoes and silk moths are terrestrial flying insects, not primarily aquatic.

items.stem: A tadpole is observed to have developed hind legs but still possesses a tail and lives in water. This stage is best described as a:

options.label: A
options.text: Fully adult frog

options.label: B
options.text: Spawn

options.label: C
options.text: Early tadpole (no legs)

options.label: D
options.text: Late tadpole or frog let

items.answer: (D) Late tadpole or frog let The development of hind legs while still having a tail signifies a later tadpole stage, which then transitions into a frog let stage as it further develops towards adulthood.

items.stem: Assertion (A) : All living beings require food. Reason (R) : Food provides energy for growth, development, and performing various life functions.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer: (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Nutrition (obtaining food) is a fundamental characteristic of life. Food supplies the necessary energy and materials for organisms to grow, develop, repair tissues, and carry out all their life processes.

items.stem: Continuous bright sunlight.

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 2 and 3 only

options.label: C
options.text: 1 and 3 only

items.answer: (A) 1 and 2 only Most seeds require adequate water, air (oxygen), and a suitable temperature for germination. While not explicitly detailed for beans , temperature is a generally accepted factor. Continuous bright sunlight is typically not required for the germination process itself for most seeds.

items.stem: Avadhi observes a plant in her garden whose leaves close up at night and open during the day. This behavior of the amla leaves is an example of the plant:

options.label: A
options.text: Performing photosynthesis only at night

options.label: B
options.text: Responding to the stimulus of changing light conditions (day/night)

options.label: C
options.text: Conserving water more effectively during the day

options.label: D
options.text: Protecting itself from nocturnal insects

items.answer: (B) Responding to the stimulus of changing light conditions (day/night). The closing and opening of leaves in response to sunset and sunrise (changes in light intensity) is a form of nastic movement, demonstrating the plant’s ability to respond to environmental stimuli.

items.stem: What is the common term for the process by which living beings produce new ones of their own kind?

options.label: A
options.text: Respiration

options.label: B
options.text: Excretion

options.label: C
options.text: Reproduction

options.label: D
options.text: Germination

items.answer: (C) Reproduction Reproduction is the biological process that results in the formation of new individual organisms, ensuring the continuation of the species.

items.stem: If a plant’s shoot grows upwards, away from the ground, this is generally a response to which two stimuli?

options.label: A
options.text: Towards gravity and away from light

options.label: B
options.text: Away from gravity (negative gravitropism) and often towards light (phototropism)

options.label: C
options.text: Towards water and towards touch

options.label: D
options.text: Away from air and towards heat

items.answer: (B) Away from gravity (negative gravitropism) and often towards light (phototropism). Plant shoots typically exhibit negative gravitropism (growing against the pull of gravity) and positive phototropism (growing towards a light source, which is essential for photosynthesis).

items.stem: What is the embryo in a seed?

options.label: A
options.text: The stored food material for the young plant

options.label: B
options.text: The protective outer layer of the seed

options.label: C
options.text: The tiny, undeveloped plant contained within the seed

options.label: D
options.text: The first root that emerges from the seed

items.answer: (C) The tiny, undeveloped plant contained within the seed. The embryo is the core part of a seed, representing a miniature, dormant plant that has the potential to develop into a seedling under favorable conditions.

items.stem: In the life cycle of a frog, which stage immediately follows the tadpole with legs stage, before becoming a fully adult frog?

options.label: A
options.text: Spawn

options.label: B
options.text: Embryo

options.label: C
options.text: Frog let

options.label: D
options.text: Pupa

items.answer: (C) Frog let The life cycle where the tadpole with legs develops into a frog let (a young frog that may still have a tail stub) before maturing into an adult frog.

items.stem: How does respiration in most animals (like humans) differ from how plants primarily exchange gases with the atmosphere?

options.label: A
options.text: Animals inhale oxygen and exhale carbon dioxide; plants do the opposite

options.label: B
options.text: Animals use lungs/gills for gas exchange; plants use stomata on leaves

options.label: C
options.text: Animals respire only during the day; plants respire only at night

options.label: D
options.text: Animals do not respire; only plants do

items.answer: (B) Animals use lungs/gills for gas exchange; plants use stomata on leaves. While both respire (take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide for energy), animals typically have specialized respiratory organs like lungs or gills. Plants primarily exchange gases through tiny pores called stomata on their leaves.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the pupal stage of a mosquito?

options.label: A
options.text: It is an aquatic stage

options.label: B
options.text: It is a non-feeding stage

options.label: C
options.text: The adult mosquito emerges from it

options.label: D
options.text: It actively flies to find food

items.answer: (D) It actively flies to find food. The pupa is an aquatic, non-feeding, and relatively immobile transformation stage. The adult, flying mosquito emerges from the pupa.

items.stem: A student wants to investigate if bean seeds need air for germination. They set up two pots: Pot X with moist soil and seeds, left open to air; Pot Y with moist soil and seeds, covered with a thick layer of oil to block air. What would be a likely observation after a few days?

options.label: A
options.text: Seeds in both pots will germinate equally well

options.label: B
options.text: Seeds in Pot X will germinate, while seeds in Pot Y will not (or germinate poorly)

options.label: C
options.text: Seeds in Pot Y will germinate, while seeds in Pot X will not

options.label: D
options.text: Neither pot will show germination as oil is harmful

items.answer: (B) Seeds in Pot X will germinate, while seeds in Pot Y will not (or germinate poorly). Air (specifically oxygen) is necessary for seed respiration during germination. Blocking air supply with a layer of oil would inhibit this process in Pot Y, while seeds in Pot X have access to air.

items.stem: Assertion (A) : Most plants are considered living beings. Reason (R) : Plants show characteristics such as growth, response to stimuli, and reproduction.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer: (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Plants are classified as living because they exhibit the key characteristics that define life, including the ability to grow, respond to environmental changes, and produce offspring.

items.stem: Process of respiration.

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 1 and 3 only

options.label: C
options.text: 2 and 3 only

items.answer: (B) 1 and 3 only Both plants and animals require nutrition and respire to live. While animals typically exhibit locomotion, most plants are stationary, though they do show other forms of movement.

items.stem: A farmer plants some seeds in a field. After a few days, tiny green shoots emerge from the soil. This initial emergence and development of the young plant from the seed is known as:

options.label: A
options.text: Pollination

options.label: B
options.text: Fertilization

options.label: C
options.text: Germination

options.label: D
options.text: Photosynthesis

items.answer: (C) Germination Germination is the process by which an organism grows from a seed or similar structure. The emergence of shoots from the soil is a clear indication that the seeds have germinated and begun to grow.

items.stem: What is the outer covering of a seed called?
items.answer: Seed coat

items.stem: What are the tiny pores on the surface of leaves called?
items.answer: Stomata

items.stem: What is the process of producing new ones of one’s own kind called?
items.answer: Reproduction

items.stem: Name an insectivorous plant mentioned in the chapter.
items.answer: Drosera

items.stem: What is the jelly-like cluster of frog eggs known as?
items.answer: Spawn

items.stem: Who built the machine called crescograph?
items.answer: Jagadish Chandra Bose

items.stem: What is the initial stage of a mosquito’s life cycle after the egg?
items.answer: Larva

items.stem: What do plants excrete in the form of small droplets on leaves?
items.answer: Excess water and minerals

items.stem: What is the term for any event that prompts living beings to respond?
items.answer: Stimulus

items.stem: What is the process of removing waste products from the body called?
items.answer: Excretion

items.stem: What is the process of taking air in and out called?
items.answer: Breathing

items.stem: What does water soften in a seed during germination?
items.answer: Seed coat

items.stem: Which part of a plant generally grows downwards?
items.answer: Root

items.stem: What stage comes after the tadpole with tail in a frog’s life cycle?
items.answer: Tadpole with legs

items.stem: What type of plant folds its leaves when touched?
items.answer: Touch-me-not (Mimosa/Chhui-mui)

items.stem: What material is secreted by silk moth larvae?
items.answer: Thread-like material (silk fibre)

items.stem: What helps tadpoles swim in water?
items.answer: Tails

items.stem: Name a disease transmitted by female mosquitoes.
items.answer: Malaria

items.stem: What is the final stage of a plant’s life cycle?
items.answer: Death

items.stem: What is the movement seen in climbers?
items.answer: Winding around objects

items.stem: What stage follows the egg stage in a frog’s life cycle?
items.answer: Embryo

items.stem: What is urine an example of in animals?
items.answer: Excretion product

items.stem: Which scientist experimented with plants’ responses to stimuli?
items.answer: Jagadish Chandra Bose

items.stem: What is the term for a seed turning into a sprout?
items.answer: Germination

items.stem: What condition is not essential for the germination of most seeds?
items.answer: Light

items.stem: Why is it advised not to allow water to stagnate in our surroundings?
items.answer: Stagnant water provides breeding grounds for mosquitoes, which can transmit diseases like malaria and dengue. Preventing stagnation disrupts their life cycle.

items.stem: Explain how a car is different from a living being, even though both can move.
items.answer: A car’s movement is not internal or self-initiated, and it does not exhibit other living characteristics like growth, reproduction, or respiration, unlike living beings.

items.stem: How do plants show movement, even though they don’t move from one place to another?
items.answer: Plants show movements like the opening of flowers, the inward movement of hair in insectivorous plants like Drosera, and climbers winding around objects.

items.stem: What is the purpose of the sticky ends on the hair-like projections of a Drosera plant?
items.answer: The sticky ends trap insects, which the Drosera plant then uses for nutrition, as it is an insectivorous plant dependent on insects.

items.stem: Why is respiration considered an essential characteristic of all living beings?
items.answer: Respiration is essential because it is the process through which living beings take in air and release it, converting food into energy necessary for survival.

items.stem: Briefly explain the phenomenon of excretion in plants with an example.
items.answer: Plants excrete excess water and minerals, which can be observed as small droplets on the leaves of plants like grasses and roses.

items.stem: What is a stimulus, and provide two examples of how living beings respond to stimuli?
items.answer: A stimulus is anything that prompts a living being to respond. Examples include reacting to stepping on a thorn or the folding of leaves in a touch-me-not plant when touched.

items.stem: Why is reproduction necessary for living beings?
items.answer: Reproduction is necessary for the continuity of life, ensuring that new individuals of their own kind are produced and the species survives across generations.

items.stem: What are the three essential conditions required for the germination of most seeds?
items.answer: The three essential conditions for the germination of most seeds are the right amount of water, air, and suitable light and/or dark conditions.

items.stem: How does water help in the process of seed germination?
items.answer: Water is crucial as it enables necessary processes for growth, softens the seed coat, and helps the tiny embryo inside develop into a plant.

items.stem: Why is air important for seed germination?
items.answer: Seeds need air for germination, as they utilize the air present in the spaces between soil particles. These spaces also facilitate root growth.

items.stem: Does light always inhibit seed germination? Explain with an example.
items.answer: No, not always. While most seeds don’t require light, some flowering plant seeds like Coleus and Petunia actually require light to germinate.

items.stem: Describe the general direction of growth for the root and shoot of a plant.
items.answer: Generally, the root of a plant grows downwards, towards the ground, while the shoot grows upwards, away from the ground and towards sunlight.

items.stem: What is the life cycle of a plant?
items.answer: The life cycle of a plant is the entire process from a seed growing into a young plant, maturing to produce flowers and fruit, and then forming new seeds, which continue the cycle.

items.stem: What are the four stages in the life cycle of a mosquito?
items.answer: The four stages in the life cycle of a mosquito are egg, larva, pupa, and adult.

items.stem: How does spraying kerosene oil on stagnant water disrupt the mosquito’s life cycle?
items.answer: Kerosene oil forms a thin layer on the water surface, separating water from air. This prevents mosquito larvae and pupae from inhaling air, causing them to die.

items.stem: What are tadpoles, and where do they primarily live in the early stages?
items.answer: Tadpoles are the larval stage of a frog. In their early stages, they live entirely in water and have tails for swimming.

items.stem: Explain the transition of a tadpole to a froglet.
items.answer: Tadpoles gradually grow, developing legs while still retaining their tails. They start to resemble small frogs, known as froglets, and begin to spend some time on land.

items.stem: How do adult frogs differ from froglets in terms of habitat and physical features?
items.answer: Adult frogs lose their tails completely and develop strong legs for jumping. Unlike froglets which still spend time in water, adult frogs live both in water and on land.

items.stem: What is the significance of the significant changes observed in the life cycles of animals like mosquitoes and frogs?
items.answer: These significant changes, involving body shape, structure and sometimes habitat, are important for the survival of the species and for maintaining the continuity of their kind.

items.stem: What is the role of the seed coat during seed germination?
items.answer: The seed coat is the outer covering of the seed, and water helps soften it, allowing the tiny embryo inside to develop and emerge.

items.stem: Why do mosquito larvae and pupae repeatedly come to the water surface?
items.answer: Mosquito larvae and pupae, although living in water, require air to respire, so they frequently come to the water surface to breathe.

items.stem: What does it mean when a living being is considered “dead”?
items.answer: A living being is considered dead when it is no longer able to exhibit the essential characteristics of life, such as movement, growth, or reproduction, even with necessary resources.

items.stem: How do the spaces between soil particles assist plant growth?
items.answer: The spaces between soil particles not only provide air for seed germination but also allow the roots of the growing plant to expand and grow easily.

items.stem: What is the ‘spawn’ in the life cycle of a frog?
items.answer: Spawn refers to the white, jelly-like substance, typically found on the water surface near pond edges, which is actually a cluster of frog eggs.

items.stem: Discuss the various characteristics that differentiate living beings from non-living things.
items.answer: Living beings are distinct from non-living things due to several characteristics. They exhibit movement, require food for nutrition and growth, respire by taking in and giving out air, excrete waste products, respond to stimuli, reproduce to create new ones of their kind, and eventually die. The absence of any of these features generally indicates a non-living entity.

items.stem: Explain how plants, despite being stationary, demonstrate movement. Provide specific examples.
items.answer: Although plants do not move from one place to another, they exhibit various forms of movement. Examples include the opening of flowers, the inward movement of hair-like projections in insectivorous plants like Drosera to trap insects, and climbers winding themselves around nearby objects. These movements are often responses to external stimuli or part of their growth process.

items.stem: Describe the role of Jagadish Chandra Bose in understanding plant responses.
items.answer: Jagadish Chandra Bose was an Indian scientist who conducted pioneering experiments with plants. He invented the crescograph, a machine capable of recording plant responses to stimuli such as light, heat, electricity and gravity. Through his work, he successfully demonstrated that plants are indeed capable of sensing and responding to various environmental cues.

items.stem: Elaborate on the essential conditions required for seed germination and their importance.
items.answer: For seed germination, the essential conditions are the right amount of water and air. Water is vital as it enables internal processes for growth and softens the seed coat, allowing the embryo to develop. Air, specifically oxygen, is required for respiration by the embryo, which obtains it from spaces between soil particles. While light is generally not essential for most seeds to germinate, it becomes crucial for the seedling’s further growth after germination.

items.stem: Design a simple experiment to determine if sunlight is necessary for seed germination.
items.answer: Take two identical pots with moist soil and sow bean seeds in both. Place one pot in direct sunlight and the other in a completely dark location (e.g., a cupboard), ensuring both receive sufficient water. Observe for 7-10 days. If seeds germinate in the dark pot, it suggests sunlight is not essential. If they only germinate in the light, it indicates sunlight is needed.

items.stem: Explain the concept of response to stimuli in living beings, providing examples for both animals and plants.
items.answer: Response to stimuli is a fundamental characteristic of living beings, where they react to any change in their environment. For animals, an immediate withdrawal of a foot after stepping on a sharp object like a thorn is a direct response. In plants, the touch-me-not plant folding its leaves when touched, or certain plants folding leaves after sunset, exemplify their response to touch and light stimuli respectively.

items.stem: Describe the life cycle of a bean plant, highlighting its key stages.
items.answer: The life cycle of a bean plant begins with a seed (Stage I) which undergoes germination (Stage II) with suitable conditions, forming a sprout. This is followed by the appearance of leaves (Stage III), then flowers (Stage IV) and finally fruits (Stage V), which are pods containing new seeds. After fruit formation, the plant gradually dries and dies, but the seeds ensure the continuity of the next generation.

items.stem: Compare and contrast the life cycles of a mosquito and a frog.
items.answer: Both mosquitoes and frogs undergo metamorphosis, having distinct larval and pupal stages before becoming adults. Mosquitoes go through egg, larva, pupa and adult stages, with larvae and pupae being aquatic. Frogs have egg (spawn), embryo, tadpole (with and without legs), froglet and adult stages. Tadpoles are aquatic and herbivorous, while adult frogs are amphibious. A key difference is the mode of reproduction (eggs laid on water surface by mosquitoes vs. jelly-like spawn by frogs) and the specific forms of their larval and pupal stages.

items.stem: Explain the concept of “death” in living beings within the context of their life cycle.
items.answer: Death in living beings signifies the cessation of all life activities, even when essential resources like food, air, and water are available. It marks the end of their life cycle, where they are no longer able to exhibit characteristics such as growth, movement, respiration, or reproduction. For plants, this can be seen when they stop growing, turn yellow, and dry after fruiting.

items.stem: Describe the changes a frog undergoes from its egg stage to an adult frog.
items.answer: The frog’s life begins as eggs, known as spawn, laid in water. These eggs develop into embryos. The embryo hatches into a tadpole, which initially has a tail for swimming and no legs. As it grows, the tadpole develops hind legs, then forelegs. This stage is followed by the froglet, which still has a tail but also legs and starts to spend time on land. Finally, the tail disappears completely, and the froglet transforms into an adult frog, capable of living both in water and on land.

items.stem: How does gravity influence the growth direction of a plant’s root and shoot?
items.answer: Gravity plays a crucial role in directing plant growth. Roots exhibit positive gravitropism, meaning they grow downwards in response to gravity, regardless of the plant’s orientation. Shoots, on the other hand, exhibit negative gravitropism, growing upwards against the force of gravity. This ensures proper anchorage and access to sunlight for the plant.

items.stem: Explain the term ‘respiration’ in both animals and plants. How is it similar and different?
items.answer: Respiration is the process by which all living beings exchange gases to release energy. In animals, like humans, it involves inhaling air (oxygen) and exhaling (carbon dioxide and water vapor) through organs like lungs. In plants, respiration occurs through tiny pores called stomata on leaves, where they take in air and release it. While both processes involve gas exchange for energy, the mechanisms and structures involved differ significantly.

items.stem: Discuss how the observation of movement can sometimes be misleading when classifying living and non-living things.
items.answer: Movement can be a deceptive characteristic because some non-living things, like cars, also move. However, their movement is externally driven, unlike living beings that move on their own. Conversely, some living beings, like plants, do not move from one place to another but show other forms of movement, such as flower opening or bending towards light. Therefore, movement alone is not sufficient to distinguish living from non-living.

items.stem: What is the significance of the life cycle in ensuring the continuity of a species, both for plants and animals?
items.answer: The life cycle is crucial for the continuity of a species as it ensures the production of new generations. For plants, seeds lead to new plants that mature, flower, and produce more seeds. For animals, reproduction leads to offspring that grow through various stages to become adults, capable of reproducing themselves. This continuous cycle prevents the extinction of the species and maintains biodiversity.

items.stem: Avadhi wants to grow some bean plants. She takes a pot filled with garden soil and sows bean seeds. She places the pot on her balcony where it receives plenty of sunlight. However, after two weeks, she notices that none of the seeds have germinated. She is puzzled because she thought sunlight was essential for plant growth. (i) What crucial condition did Avadhi likely miss for the seeds to germinate? (ii) Explain why sunlight is not usually essential for seed germination, but water is. (iii) What should Avadhi do to ensure her bean seeds germinate successfully?
items.answer: (i) Avadhi likely missed providing sufficient water to the seeds for germination. (ii) Most seeds do not require light for germination; instead, water is crucial as it softens the seed coat and activates the internal processes necessary for the embryo’s development into a sprout. (iii) Avadhi should ensure the soil in her pot is kept moderately moist by adding a regular and sufficient amount of water.

items.stem: Aayush is on a nature walk with his class and observes a unique plant. When he accidentally brushes against its leaves, they immediately fold inwards. The teacher explains that this plant is very sensitive to touch. Later, he also sees some plants with sticky, hair-like structures on their leaves, and the teacher mentions they trap insects. (i) What characteristic of living beings is demonstrated by the plant whose leaves fold inwards? (ii) Name the type of plant that has sticky, hair- like structures and traps insects. Why do they do this? (iii) Are these movements in plants considered movement in the same way an animal moves? Explain.
items.answer: (i) The plant demonstrates the characteristic of responding to stimuli. (ii) The plant is an insectivorous plant, like Drosera. They trap insects for nutrition because they are dependent on insects for it. (iii) No, these are specific types of movements within the plant, such as folding leaves or winding, unlike an animal’s ability to move from one place to another.

items.stem: During the rainy season, the local community is advised to prevent water stagnation to control mosquito populations. A resident is seen spraying kerosene oil on a small collection of stagnant water in a discarded tire. Another resident suggests covering all water containers. (i) Why is preventing water stagnation crucial for controlling mosquitoes? (ii) How does spraying kerosene oil on stagnant water help disrupt the mosquito life cycle? (Explaining) (iii) What stages of the mosquito life cycle are directly affected by these measures? (Applying)
items.answer: (i) Preventing water stagnation is crucial because mosquitoes lay their eggs in stagnant water, which serves as a breeding ground for them. (ii) Kerosene oil forms a thin layer on the water surface, blocking the larvae and pupae from accessing air needed for respiration, causing them to die. (iii) The egg, larval, and pupal stages are directly affected, as these stages are dependent on stagnant water for development and respiration.

items.stem: Avadhi looks at a picture of herself from four years ago and notices how much she has changed. She tries to wear a dress from that time, but it no longer fits her. Her mother explains that this is because she has grown. (i) What fundamental characteristic of living beings is illustrated by Avadhi’s inability to wear her old dress? (Applying) (ii) Do non-living things also exhibit this characteristic? Give an example to support your answer. (iii) Besides growth, what other key characteristic supports the idea that Avadhi is a living being?
items.answer: (i) This illustrates the fundamental characteristic of growth in living beings. (ii) No, non-living things do not exhibit true growth. For example, a car does not grow in size; it only appears to “grow” through additions, not internal biological processes. (iii) Besides growth, Avadhi also shows movement, respiration, needs food, excretes, responds to stimuli, and can reproduce in the future.

items.stem: During a school trip to a pond, students observe white, jelly-like clusters floating on the water surface. Upon closer inspection, they also see small, fish-like creatures swimming, some with tiny legs emerging. The teacher explains that these are different stages of a frog’s life. (i) What is the scientific name for the white, jelly-like clusters of frog eggs? (ii) What are the small, fish-like creatures swimming in the water called, and what do they use to move? (iii) Describe the habitat change a frog undergoes during its life cycle from the observed stages to an adult.
items.answer: (i) The white, jelly-like clusters of frog eggs are called spawn. (ii) The small, fish-like creatures are tadpoles, and they use their tails to swim in the water. (iii) Tadpoles and froglets initially live mostly in water. As they mature into adult frogs, they develop strong legs and lose their tails, becoming capable of living both in water and on land.
